<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in"><span style="font-size: 7pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">The goodwill is attributed to the Proprietary
Products segment, which represent the lowest level within the Company at which goodwill is monitored for internal management purposes.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify"><span style="font-size: 7pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">Impairment test of goodwill for the
year ended on December 31, 2024:</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify"><span style="font-size: 7pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">Impairment loss for goodwill is recognized
if the recoverable amount of the goodwill is less than the carrying amount. The recoverable amount is the greater of fair value less
costs of disposal, or value in use of the relevant reporting level (i.e., a CGU of a group of CGUs).</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify"><span style="font-size: 7pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">The Company performed an assessment
for goodwill impairment for its Proprietary Products segment, which is the level at which goodwill is monitored for internal management
purposes and concluded that the fair value of the Proprietary Products segment exceeds the carrying amount by approximately <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c0" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:IntangibleAssetCarryingAmountPercentage" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-31955">24</ix:nonFraction>%. The
carrying amount of goodwill assigned to this segment is in the amount of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c2" decimals="-3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:IntangibleAssetsOtherThanGoodwillCarryingAmountOfRevaluedAssets" scale="3" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-31956">30,313</ix:nonFraction> thousand.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify"><span style="font-size: 7pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">When evaluating the fair value of the
Proprietary Products segment, the Company used a discounted cash flow model which utilized Level 3 measures that represent unobservable
inputs. Key assumptions used to determine the estimated fair value include: (a) internal cash flows forecasts for <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" format="ixt-sec:duryear" name="kmda:EstimatedFutureCashFlows" id="ixv-31957">5</ix:nonNumeric> years following the
assessment date, including expected revenue growth, costs to produce, operating profit margins and estimated capital needs; (b) an estimated
terminal value using a terminal year long-term future growth rate of -<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c0" decimals="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:longTermFutureGrowthRate" scale="-2" sign="-" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-31958">5.0</ix:nonFraction>% determined based on the long-term expected prospects of the
reporting unit; and (c) a discount rate (post-tax) of <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c0" decimals="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:weightedaverageCostOfCapital" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-31959">12.2</ix:nonFraction> % which reflects the weighted-average cost of capital adjusted for the relevant
risk associated with the Proprietary Products segment&#8217;s operations.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify"><span style="font-size: 7pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">Actual results may differ from those
assumed in the Company&#8217;s valuation method. It is reasonably possible that the Company&#8217;s assumptions described above could
change in future periods. If any of these were to vary materially from the Company&#8217;s plans, it may record impairment of goodwill
allocated to this reporting unit in the future. A hypothetical decrease in the growth rate of <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c0" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:GrowthRate" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-31960">1</ix:nonFraction>% or an increase of <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c2" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:DiscountRate" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-31961">1</ix:nonFraction>% to the discount
rate would have reduced the fair value of the Proprietary Products segment by approximately $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c60" decimals="-3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:ProprietaryProductsSegment" scale="3" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-31962">5,142</ix:nonFraction> thousand and $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c61" decimals="-3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:ProprietaryProductsSegment" scale="3" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-31963">21,164</ix:nonFraction> thousand, respectively.</p></ix:continuation><div>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Lease extension</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in">The Company has leases that include extension options. These
options provide flexibility in managing the leased assets and align with the Company&#8217;s business needs.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in">The Company exercises judgement in deciding whether it is
reasonably certain that the extension options will be exercised.</p></ix:continuation><div>

</div><ix:continuation id="_DisclosureOfLeasesExplanatory-c0_cont_2"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">The lease agreement entered into by Kamada
Plasma LLC for the premises in Houston, Texas and in San Antonio, Texas to be used as a plasma collection center includes an option
to extend the lease as follow:</p>

                                            for two consecutive periods of five years each, upon 120 days prior written notice.</td></tr></table>

<p style="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; border-spacing: 0px;"><tr style="vertical-align: top">

                                            three consecutive periods of five years each, upon at least 120 days prior written notice.</td></tr></table>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><span style="font-variant: small-caps"><b>Note 15: - Financial Instruments
(Cont.)</b></span></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>&#160;</b></p><div>

</div><ix:continuation continuedAt="_DisclosureOfFinancialInstrumentsExplanatory-c0_cont_2" id="_DisclosureOfFinancialInstrumentsExplanatory-c0_cont_1"><table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 0.5in">&#160;</td>
    <td style="width: 0.5in"><span style="font-size: 10pt">b.</span></td>
    <td><span style="font-size: 10pt"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Financial risk factors</span></span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">The Company&#8217;s activities expose
it to various financial risks, such as market risk (foreign currency risk, interest rate risk and price risk), credit risk and liquidity
risk. The Company&#8217;s investment policy focuses on activities that will preserve the Company&#8217;s capital. The Company utilizes
derivatives to hedge certain exposures to risk.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">Risk management is the responsibility
of the Company&#8217;s management and specifically that of the Company&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and Chief Financial Officer
(CFO), in accordance with the policy approved by the Board of Directors. The Board of Directors provides principles for the overall risk
management.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 1in">&#160;</td>
    <td style="width: 0.5in"><span style="font-size: 10pt">1.</span></td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-size: 10pt"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Market risks</span></span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 1.5in">&#160;</td>
    <td><span style="font-size: 10pt"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Foreign exchange risk</span></span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1.5in; text-align: justify">The Company operates in an international
environment and is exposed to foreign exchange risk resulting from the exposure to different currencies, mainly the NIS and EUR. Foreign
exchange risks arise from recognized assets and liabilities denominated in a foreign currency other than the functional currency, such
as trade and other accounts receivables, trade and other accounts payables, loans and capital leases.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1.5in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1.5in; text-align: justify">As of December 31, 2024, and 2023,
the Company held financial derivatives intended to hedge changes in the exchange rate of the USD vs. the NIS and the EUR (see also Note
15f. below).</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 1in">&#160;</td>
    <td style="width: 0.5in"><span style="font-size: 10pt">2.</span></td>
    <td><span style="font-size: 10pt"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Credit risk</span></span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1.5in; text-align: justify">Financial instruments that potentially
subject the Company to concentrations of credit risk consist principally of cash and cash equivalents, short-term bank deposits, trade
receivables and foreign currency derivative contracts.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 1.5in">&#160;</td>
    <td style="width: 0.5in"><span style="font-size: 10pt">a)</span></td>
    <td><span style="font-size: 10pt"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Cash, cash equivalent and short-term investments:</span></span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 2in; text-align: justify">The Company holds cash, cash equivalents,
short term deposits and other financial instruments at major financial institutions in Israel and the United States. In accordance with
Company policy, evaluations of the relative strength of credit of the various financial institutions are made on an ongoing basis.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1.5in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 2in; text-align: justify">Short-term investments include short-term
deposits with low risk for a period less than one year.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1.5in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 1.5in">&#160;</td>
    <td style="width: 0.5in"><span style="font-size: 10pt">b)</span></td>
    <td><span style="font-size: 10pt"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Trade receivables:</span></span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 2in; text-align: justify">The Company regularly monitors the credit
extended to its customers and their general financial condition, and, when necessary, requires collateral as security for the debt such
as letters of creditor and down payments. In addition, the Company partially insures its non-Israeli based accounts receivables with foreign
trade risk insurance. Refer to Note 6 for additional information.</p></ix:continuation><div>

</div><ix:continuation continuedAt="_DisclosureOfFinancialInstrumentsExplanatory-c0_cont_3" id="_DisclosureOfFinancialInstrumentsExplanatory-c0_cont_2"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 2in; text-align: justify">The Company keeps constant track of customer
debt, and, to the extent required, accounts for an allowance for expected credit losses that adequately reflects, in the Company&#8217;s
assessment, the loss embodied in the debts the collection of which is in doubt.</p>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1.5in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 2in; text-align: justify">The Company&#8217;s maximum exposure
to credit risk for the components of the statement of financial position as of December 31, 2024, and 2023 is the carrying amount of
trade receivables.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1.5in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">

    <td style="width: 0.5in"><span style="font-size: 10pt">c)</span></td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-size: 10pt"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Foreign currency derivative contracts:</span></span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 2in; text-align: justify">The Company is exposed to foreign currency
exchange fluctuations, primarily in USD vs. NIS and EUR. Consequently, it enters into various foreign currency exchange contracts with
major Israeli financial institutions (see also Note 15f. below).</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 2in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 1.5in">&#160;</td>
    <td style="width: 0.5in"><span style="font-size: 10pt">d)</span></td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-size: 10pt"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Interest rate risk:</span></span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 2in; text-align: justify">Interest rate risk is the risk that
the fair value or future cash flows of a financial instrument will fluctuate because of changes in market interest rates. The Company&#8217;s
exposure to the risk of changes in market interest rates relates primarily to the Company&#8217;s long-term liabilities.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;">

  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

was based on standard pricing valuation model such as a discounted cash-flow model which considers the present value of future cash flows
discounted by an interest rate that reflects market conditions (Level 3).</p>

equivalents, short-term bank deposits, trade and other receivables, trade and other payables approximates their fair value, due to the
short-term maturities of the financial instruments.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 56.7pt; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">During 2024 and 2023 there was no transfer
due to the fair value measurement of any financial instrument from Level 1 to Level 2, and furthermore, there were no transfers to or
from Level 3 due to the fair value measurement of any financial instrument.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Sensitivity tests and principal
work assumptions</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">The selected changes in the relevant
risk variables were determined based on management&#8217;s estimate as to reasonable possible changes in these risk variables.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">The Company has performed sensitivity
tests of principal market risk factors that are liable to affect its reported operating results or financial position. The sensitivity
tests present the profit or loss in respect of each financial instrument for the relevant risk variable chosen for that instrument as
of each reporting date. <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" continuedAt="_SensitivityAnalysisForEachTypeOfMarketRisk-c0_cont_1" escape="true" name="ifrs-full:SensitivityAnalysisForEachTypeOfMarketRisk" id="ixv-32278">The test of risk factors was determined based on the materiality of the exposure of the operating results or
financial condition of each risk with reference to the functional currency and assuming that all the other variables are constant.</ix:nonNumeric></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Derivatives instruments not designated as hedging </span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 85.05pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: -28.35pt">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">The Company has foreign currency forward contracts designed to protect
it from exposure to fluctuations in exchange rates, mainly of NIS and EUR, in respect of its trade receivables, trade payables. Foreign
currency forward contracts are not designated as cash flow hedges, fair value or net investment in a foreign operation. These derivatives
are not considered as hedge accounting. As of December 31, 2024, and December 31, 2023, the fair value of the derivative instruments not
designated as hedging was a financial liability of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c2" decimals="-3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:DerivativeFinancialLiabilities" scale="3" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-32301">10</ix:nonFraction> thousand and financial asset of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c2" decimals="-3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:DerivativeFinancialAssets" scale="3" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-32302">8</ix:nonFraction> thousand, respectively. The open transactions
(Derivative contract which have not yet been settled) for those derivatives were in an amount of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c93" decimals="-3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:OpenTransactionsForDerivativeInstrumentsNotDesignatedAsHedging" scale="3" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-32303">3,652</ix:nonFraction> thousands and $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c94" decimals="-3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:OpenTransactionsForDerivativeInstrumentsNotDesignatedAsHedging" scale="3" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-32304">9,149</ix:nonFraction> thousands,
respectively.</p>

</div><ix:continuation continuedAt="_DisclosureOfNetDefinedBenefitLiabilityAssetExplanatory-c0_cont_2" id="_DisclosureOfNetDefinedBenefitLiabilityAssetExplanatory-c0_cont_1"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">Employee benefits consist of short-term
benefits and post-employment benefits.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">Post-employment benefits:</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">According to the Israeli labor and Severance
Pay Laws, the Company is required to pay compensation to employees upon dismissal or retirement or to make contributions in defined contribution
plans pursuant to Section 14 of the Israeli Severance Pay Law, as specified below. The Company&#8217;s liability is accounted for as a
post-employment benefit only for those employees for which Section 14 of the Israeli Severance Pay Law is not applicable to. The computation
of the Company&#8217;s employee benefit liability is made in accordance with a valid employment contract, or a collective bargaining agreement
based on the employee&#8217;s salary and employment terms which establish the entitlement to receive the compensation.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">The post-employment employee benefits
are normally financed by contributions classified as defined benefit plans, as detailed below:</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.65in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;">

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1.5in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1.5in; text-align: justify">The Company&#8217;s agreements with some
of its employees are in accordance with Section 14 of the Israeli Severance Pay Law. Contributions made by the Company in accordance with

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 85.05pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: -28.35pt">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;"> <tr style="vertical-align: top"> <td style="width: 0.5in">&#160;</td> <td style="width: 0.5in"><span style="font-size: 10pt">a.</span></td> <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-size: 10pt">On August 23, 2010, the Company entered into a <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c432" format="ixt-sec:duryear" name="kmda:AgreementTerm" id="ixv-32391">30</ix:nonNumeric>-year collaboration agreement with Baxter Healthcare Corporation (&#8220;Baxter&#8221;) with respect for granting of the distribution rights for GLASSIA. During 2015, Baxter assigned all its rights under the collaboration agreement to Baxalta US Inc. (&#8220;Baxalta&#8221;) which was acquired during 2016 by Shire plc. (&#8220;Shire&#8221;), which is now part of Takeda (&#8220;Takeda&#8221; and in these consolidated financial statements Baxter, Baxalta and Shire will be referred to as &#8220;Takeda&#8221;).</span></td></tr> </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1.25in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">The collaboration agreement consists
of three main agreements (1) an Exclusive Manufacturing, Supply and Distribution agreement for GLASSIA in the United States, Canada,
Australia and New Zealand (the &#8220;Territory&#8221; and the &#8220;Distribution Agreement&#8221;, respectively); (2) Technology License
Agreement for the use of the Company&#8217;s knowhow and patents for the production, continued development and sale of GLASSIA by Takeda
(the &#8220;License Agreement&#8221;) in the Territory; and (3) A Paste Supply Agreement for the supply by Takeda of plasma derived fraction
IV-1 to be used by the Company for the production of GLASSIA (the &#8220;Raw Materials Supply Agreement&#8221;).</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">Pursuant to the agreements, the
Company was entitled to certain upfront and milestone payments at a total amount of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c433" decimals="-6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:AgreementPaymentAmount" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-32392">45</ix:nonFraction> million, all of which were received and
accounted for as income through December 31, 2021, and for a minimum commitment of Takeda to acquire GLASSIA produced by the Company
over the term of the Distribution Agreement. In addition, upon initiation of sales of GLASSIA manufactured by Takeda, the Company
would be entitled to royalty payments at a rate of <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c2" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:RoyaltyPaymentsPercentgae" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-32393">12</ix:nonFraction>% on net sales of Glassia through August 2025, and at a rate of <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c2" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:RoyaltyPaymentsPercentgaeThereafter" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-32394">6</ix:nonFraction>% thereafter
until 2040, with a minimum of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c0" decimals="-6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:RoyaltyExpense" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-32395">5</ix:nonFraction> million annually (the &#8220;Royalty Payments&#8221;).</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">During 2021, the Company terminated the production and supply of GLASSIA
to Takeda and Takeda initiated its own production of the product for distribution in the territory. In addition, during 2022, the Company
transferred to Takeda the U.S. Biologics License Application (BLA) of the product, in consideration for a $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c434" decimals="-6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:AmountReceivedFromDistributionAgreement" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-32396">2</ix:nonFraction> million payment from Takeda,
which was paid by Takeda and accounted for as income during the first quarter of 2022.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">Commencing 2022, the Company collected royalty payments from Takeda
(per the agreement term as described above). For the years ended December 31, 2024, 2023 and 2022 the Company accounted for a total of
$<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c0" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:RoyaltyIncome" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-32397">16.9</ix:nonFraction> million, $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c4" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:RoyaltyIncome" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-32398">16.1</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c5" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:RoyaltyIncome" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-32399">12.2</ix:nonFraction> million from sales-based royalty income from Takeda, respectively.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">Pursuant to the Distribution Agreement,
Takeda is responsible to conduct any required additional clinical studies required to obtain or maintain GLASSIA&#8217;s marketing authorization
in the Territory. Under certain conditions, the Company will be required to participate in the funding of these clinical studies in a
total amount not to exceed $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c433" decimals="-6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:MaximumCostOfExperimentWithThirdParty" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-32400">10</ix:nonFraction> million.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">Pursuant to the Raw Material Supply Agreement
Takeda undertook to provide the Company, free of charge, all quantities of plasma derived fraction IV-1 required by the Company for manufacturing
GLASSIA to be sold to Takeda for distribution in the Territory. The Company accounted for the fair value of the plasma derived fraction
IV-1 used and sold as revenues and charges the same fair value to cost of revenue. In addition, the Company has the right to acquire from
Takeda plasma derived fraction IV-1 for its continued development and for the production, sale and distribution of GLASSIA by the Company
outside the Territory.</p></ix:nonNumeric><div>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">During 2024 and 2023, <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c440" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:NumberOfShareOptionsExercisedInSharebasedPaymentArrangements" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-32428">189,154</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c441" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:NumberOfShareOptionsExercisedInSharebasedPaymentArrangements" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-32429">42,175</ix:nonFraction>
share options, respectively, were exercised, on a net exercise basis, into <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c442" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:NumberOfShareOptionsExercisedInSharebasedPaymentArrangement" scale="0" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-32430">23,628</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c443" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:NumberOfShareOptionsExercisedInSharebasedPaymentArrangement" scale="0" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-32431">2,662</ix:nonFraction> ordinary shares of NIS <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c444" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:ParValuePerShare" scale="0" unitRef="ilsPershares" id="ixv-32432">1</ix:nonFraction> par value each and
<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c444" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:NumberOfOutstandingBalanceShareOption" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-32433">1,875</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c445" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:NumberOfOutstandingBalanceShareOption" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-32434">12,444</ix:nonFraction> restricted shares units were vested, respectively. for 2024 and 2023, respectively.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">The Company&#8217;s goals in its capital
management are to preserve capital ratios that will ensure stability and liquidity to support business activity and create maximum value
for shareholders.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 82.4pt">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">On November 21, 2019, FIMI, the leading
private equity firm in Israel acquired from third parties <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c446" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:NumberOfSharesIssued" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-32437">5,240,956</ix:nonFraction> ordinary shares at a price of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c446" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:ParValuePerShare" scale="0" unitRef="usdPershares" id="ixv-32438">6.00</ix:nonFraction>, representing ownership of approximately
<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c447" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:ProportionOfOwnershipInterestInAssociate" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-32439">13</ix:nonFraction>% of the Company&#8217;s then outstanding shares.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">On February 10, 2020, the Company consummated
a private placement with FIMI, pursuant to which the Company issued <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c448" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:NumberOfSharesIssued" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-32440">4,166,667</ix:nonFraction> ordinary shares at a price of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c448" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:ParValuePerShare" scale="0" unitRef="usdPershares" id="ixv-32441">6.00</ix:nonFraction> per share, for total
gross proceeds of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c449" decimals="-3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:ProceedsFromIssuingShares" scale="3" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-32442">25</ix:nonFraction>,000 thousand. Upon closing of the private placement, FIMI&#8217;s aggregate ownership represented approximately
<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c449" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:ProportionOfOwnershipInterestInAssociate" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-32443">21</ix:nonFraction>% of the Company&#8217;s then outstanding shares.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">On September 7, 2023, the Company consummated
a private placement with FIMI, pursuant to which the Company issued <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c450" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:NumberOfSharesIssued" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-32444">12,631,579</ix:nonFraction> ordinary shares at a price of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c450" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:ParValuePerShare" scale="0" unitRef="usdPershares" id="ixv-32445">4.75</ix:nonFraction> per share (which represented
the average closing price of the Company&#8217;s shares on NASDAQ during the 20 trading days prior to the date of execution of the private
placement), for total gross proceeds of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c452" decimals="-3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:ProceedsFromIssuingShares" scale="3" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-32446">60</ix:nonFraction>,000 thousand. Following the closing of the private placement, FIMI beneficially owned approximately
<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c451" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:ProportionOfOwnershipInterestInAssociate" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-32447">38</ix:nonFraction>% of the Company&#8217;s outstanding ordinary shares and became a controlling shareholder of the Company, within the meaning of the
Israeli Companies Law, 1999.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">Concurrently with the execution of
the share purchase agreement, the Company entered into an amended and restated registration rights agreement with FIMI pursuant to which,
among other things, the Company undertook to file with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission a registration statement registering
the resale of all of the ordinary shares held by FIMI, per its request, at any time commencing after the lapse of six months following
the closing of the private placement.</p>

</div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" continuedAt="_DisclosureOfSharebasedPaymentArrangementsExplanatory-c0_cont_1" escape="true" name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfSharebasedPaymentArrangementsExplanatory" id="ixv-27042"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><span style="font-variant: small-caps"><b>Note 20: - Share-Based Payment</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 56.7pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: -56.7pt"><span style="font-variant: small-caps"><b>&#160;</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">On July 24, 2011, the Company&#8217;s
Board of Directors adopted the 2011 Israeli Share Option Plan. In September 2016, the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors approved an amendment
to the plan, to include the issuance of restricted shares units (&#8220;RSU&#8221;) under the plan and renamed it the Israeli Share Award
Plan (&#8220;2011 Plan&#8221;). In August 2021, the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors approved a <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c453" format="ixt-sec:duryear" name="kmda:ExtensionOfShareOptionPlan" id="ixv-32448">10</ix:nonNumeric>-year extension of the 2011 Plan,
through August 9, 2031, and adopted a few additional amendments to the 2011 Plan. The 2011 Plan was further amended in October 2022.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">Options and RSU&#8217;s <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfVestingRequirementsForSharebasedPaymentArrangement" id="ixv-32449">granted under
the 2011 Plan, prior to January 2020, generally vest over a four-year period following the date of the grant in 13 installments: 25%
on the first anniversary of the grant date and 6.25% at the end of each quarter thereafter.</ix:nonNumeric> As of 2020, options and RSUs granted under
the 2011 Plan generally vest in four equal annual installments of <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c2" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:GrantedOptionsPercentage" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-32450">25</ix:nonFraction>% each.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">In February 2022, the Company&#8217;s
Board of Directors adopted the U.S. Taxpayer Appendix to the 2011 Plan (the &#8220;U.S. Appendix&#8221;), which provides for the grant
of options and RSU to persons who are subject to U.S. federal income tax. The U.S. Appendix provides for the grant to U.S. employees
of options that qualify as incentive stock options (&#8220;ISOs&#8221;) under the U.S. Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended. The
U.S. Appendix was approved by our shareholders at the annual general meeting held in December 2022.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;&#160;</p>

estimating the grant date fair value of equity-settled share options. The measurement was made at the grant date of equity-settled share
options.</p>

</div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" continuedAt="_DisclosureOfIncomeTaxExplanatory-c0_cont_1" escape="true" name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfIncomeTaxExplanatory" id="ixv-28361"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><span style="font-variant: small-caps"><b>Note 21: - Taxes on Income</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1.25in; text-align: justify; text-indent: -28.35pt">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 0.5in">&#160;</td>
    <td style="width: 0.5in"><span style="font-size: 10pt">a.</span></td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-size: 10pt"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Tax laws applicable to the Company</span></span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 113.4pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: -28.35pt">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Law for the Encouragement of Industry
(Taxes), 1969 </span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 113.4pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: -28.35pt">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">The Law for the Encouragement of Industry
(Taxes), 1969 (the &#8220;Encouragement of Industry Law&#8221;), provides several tax benefits for &#8220;Industrial Companies.&#8221;
Pursuant to the Encouragement of Industry Law, a company qualifies as an Industrial Company if it is a resident of Israel and at least
<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c504" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:TaxRateEffectOfForeignTaxRates" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-32618">90</ix:nonFraction>% of its income in any tax year (other than income from certain government loans) is generated from an &#8220;Industrial Enterprise&#8221;
that it owns. An Industrial Enterprise is defined as an enterprise whose principal activity, in a given tax year, is industrial activity.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">An Industrial Company is entitled to certain
tax benefits, including: (i) a deduction of the cost of purchases of patents, know-how and certain other intangible property rights (other
than goodwill) used for development or promotion of the Industrial Enterprise in equal amounts over a period of <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c505" name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfUsefulLifeIntangibleAssetsOtherThanGoodwill" id="ixv-32619">eight</ix:nonNumeric> years, beginning
from the year in which such rights were first used, (ii) the right to elect to file consolidated tax returns, under certain conditions,
with additional Israeli Industrial Companies under its control, and (iii) the right to deduct expenses related to public offerings in
equal amounts over a period of <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c504" name="kmda:PeriodOfRightToDeductExpensesRelatedToPublicOfferings" id="ixv-32620">three</ix:nonNumeric> years beginning from the year of the offering.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">Eligibility for benefits under the
Encouragement of Industry Law is not contingent upon the approval of any governmental authority. The Company believes that it currently
qualifies as an industrial company within the definition of the Industry Encouragement Law. The Company cannot confirm that the Israeli
tax authorities will agree that the Company qualifies, or, if qualified, that it will continue to qualify as an industrial company or
that the benefits described above will be available to the Company in the future.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Law for the Encouragement of Capital
Investments, 1959</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Tax benefits prior to Amendment
60</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">The Company&#8217;s facilities in Israel
have been granted Approved Enterprise status under the Law for the Encouragement of Capital Investments, 1959, commonly referred to as
the &#8220;Investment Law&#8221;. The Investment Law provides that capital investments in a production facility (or other eligible assets)
may be designated as an Approved Enterprise.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">Under the Approved Enterprise programs,
a company is eligible for certain benefits such as governmental grants and tax incentives. The benefits period is limited to the earlier
of 12 years from completion of the investment or commencement of production (&#8220;Year of Operation&#8221;), or 14 years from the year
in which the certificate of approval was obtained.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">The Company&#8217;s benefit period
under the Approved Enterprise programs ended by the end of 2017.</p></ix:nonNumeric><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: center">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><span style="font-variant: small-caps"><b>Note 21: - Taxes on Income
(Cont.)</b></span></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1.25in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p><div>

</div><table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 0.5in">&#160;</td>
    <td style="width: 0.5in"><span style="font-size: 10pt">a.</span></td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-size: 10pt"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Tax laws applicable to the Company (cont.)</span></span></td></tr>
  </table><div>
</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1.25in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p><div>

</div><ix:continuation continuedAt="_DisclosureOfIncomeTaxExplanatory-c0_cont_2" id="_DisclosureOfIncomeTaxExplanatory-c0_cont_1"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Tax benefits under Amendment 60</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">On April 1, 2005, an amendment to the
Investment Law was affected (&#8220;Amendment 60&#8221;). The amendment revised the criteria for investments qualified to receive tax
benefits. An eligible investment program under the amendment will qualify for benefits as a Privileged Enterprise (rather than the previous
terminology of Approved Enterprise).</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">In May 2012, the Company received a Tax
Ruling from the Israeli Tax Authority that its activity is an industrial activity, and the Company will be eligible for the status of
a Privileged Enterprise, provided that it meets the requirements under the ruling. Pursuant to the Tax Ruling, the Year of Election was
2009. The Company also subsequently elected 2012 as a Year of Election. Through December 31, 2023, the Company did not utilize the tax
benefits under its Privileged Enterprise and those expired at the end of 2023.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">In January 2015, the Company obtained
a ruling from the ITA pursuant to which royalties-based income related to GLASSIA will be considered &#8220;Privileged Income&#8221; (within the meaning of the Investment Law), subject
to meeting certain conditions detailed in the ruling.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">Amendment 68 to the Encouragement Law:</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">As of January 1, 2011, new legislation
amending the Investment Law was affected. Pursuant to Amendment 68 a new status of &#8220;Preferred Company&#8221; and &#8220;Preferred
Enterprise&#8221;, replacing the then existing status of &#8220;Privileged Company&#8221; and &#8220;Privileged Enterprise&#8221;. A
Preferred Company is an industrial company owning a Preferred Enterprise which meets certain conditions (including a minimum threshold
of <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c506" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:ApplicableTaxRate" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-32621">25</ix:nonFraction>% export). However, under this new legislation the requirement for a minimum investment in productive assets was cancelled.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">Under Amendment 68, a uniform corporate
tax rate will apply to all qualifying income of the Preferred Company, as opposed to the former law, which was limited to income from
the Approved Enterprises during the benefits period.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">The company believes that it satisfies the requirements of the Preferred
Company status, pursuant to Amendment 68, and while it has not yet utilized the benefits under Amendment 68, it may do so in subsequent
fiscal years.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">Amendment 73 to the Encouragement Law:</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">Amendment 73 to the Encouragement Law
also prescribes special tax tracks for technological enterprises, which became effective in 2017, as follows: Preferred technological
enterprise, which is defined in the Encouragement Law as a company that owns the enterprise and is a member of a group whose total consolidated
revenues are less than NIS <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c0" decimals="-9" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:Revenue" scale="9" unitRef="ils" id="ixv-32622">10</ix:nonFraction> billion in the tax year, will be subject to tax at a rate of <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c0" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:PercentageOfSubjectToTaxRate" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-32623">12</ix:nonFraction>% on profits deriving from intellectual
property (in development area A - a tax rate of <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c507" decimals="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:PercentageOfSubjectToTaxRate" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-32624">7.5</ix:nonFraction>%). Special preferred technological enterprise which is a member of a group whose
total consolidated revenues exceed NIS <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c508" decimals="-9" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:OtherRevenue" scale="9" unitRef="ils" id="ixv-32625">10</ix:nonFraction> billion in the tax year will be subject to tax at a rate of <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c509" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:PercentageOfSubjectToTaxRate" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-32626">6</ix:nonFraction>% on preferred income from the
enterprise, regardless of the enterprise&#8217;s geographical location. Any dividends distributed to &#8220;foreign companies&#8221;,
as defined in the Encouragement Law, deriving from income from the technological enterprises will be subject to tax at a rate of <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c508" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="kmda:PercentageOfSubjectToTaxRate" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-32627">4</ix:nonFraction>%,
subject to the conditions prescribed in Section 51Z to the Encouragement Law.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">The Company evaluated the effect of
the adoption of Amendment 73 on its tax position, and as of the date of the approval of the financial statements, the Company did not
apply for the benefits under Amendment 73. The Company may elect to apply for these benefits in the future.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1.25in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">Kamada Inc and Kamada Plasma LLC
(&#8220;US subsidiaries&#8221;) are incorporated in the United States and are subject to U.S. Federal and State tax laws and
Franchise Tax. The two subsidiaries file a joint tax return.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">On December 22, 2017, the Tax Cuts
and Jobs Act (the &#8220;Act&#8221;) was signed into law. Among other things, the Act reduces the corporate tax rate to <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c511" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:TaxRateEffectFromChangeInTaxRate" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-32629">21</ix:nonFraction>% from <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c512" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="ifrs-full:TaxRateEffectFromChangeInTaxRate" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-32630">35</ix:nonFraction>%.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">On February 16, 2022, the Company incorporated
KI Biopharma LLC, as a wholly owned subsidiary of Kamada Ltd. KI Biopharma LLC is a disregarded (tax transparent) entity for U.S. tax
purposes.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

</div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" continuedAt="_DisclosureOfEntitysReportableSegmentsExplanatory-c0_cont_1" escape="true" name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfEntitysReportableSegmentsExplanatory" id="ixv-30429"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-variant: small-caps"><b>Note
24: - Operating Segments</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 0.5in">&#160;</td>
    <td style="width: 0.5in"><span style="font-size: 10pt">a.</span></td>
    <td><span style="font-size: 10pt"><span style="text-decoration:underline">General</span></span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">The operating segments are identified
based on information that is reviewed by the chief operating decision makers (&#8220;CODM&#8221;) to make decisions about resources to
be allocated and assess its performance. Accordingly, for management purposes, the Company is organized into operating segments based
on the products and services of the business units and has <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c0" decimals="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" name="kmda:NumberOfOperatingGroups" scale="0" unitRef="segments" id="ixv-32827">two</ix:nonFraction> operating segments as follows:</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 82.4pt; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 1in">&#160;</td>
    <td style="white-space: nowrap; width: 1.25in"><span style="font-size: 10pt">Proprietary Products </span></td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><p style="margin: 0pt 0; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif">Manufacturing, sales and distribution of plasma-derived protein therapeutics.</p></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px;">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 1in">&#160;</td>
    <td style="width: 1.25in"><span style="font-size: 10pt">Distribution</span></td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-size: 10pt">Distribute imported drug products in Israel, which are manufactured
    by third parties.</span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 202.45pt; text-indent: -104.8pt">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">Segment performance is evaluated based
on revenues and gross profit in the financial statements.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">The segment results reported to the
CODM include items that are allocated directly to the segments and items that can be allocated on a reasonable basis. Items that were
not allocated, mainly the Company&#8217;s corporate office, research and development costs, sales and marketing costs, general and administrative
costs and financial costs (consisting of finance expenses and finance income and including fair value adjustments of financial instruments),
are managed on a Company basis.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">The segment liabilities do not include loans and financial liabilities
as these liabilities are managed on a Company basis. The Company&#8217;s CODM does not regularly review asset information by segments and, therefore,
the Company does not report asset or liability information by segment.</p></ix:nonNumeric><div>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">Sales to related parties are conducted
at market prices. Outstanding trade receivables due from related parties the end of the year bears no interest, and their settlement will
be in cash. For the years ended December 31, 2024, 2023 and 2022, the Company recorded no allowance for doubtful accounts for trade receivable
due from related parties.</p>

Ralf Hahn, the former Chairman of the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors, and its currently under the control of the Hahn family. Mr. Ralf Hahn&#8217;s
son, Mr. Jonathan Hahn, currently the President and a director of Tuteur, served as a director of the Company from March 2010 until November
2023.</td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1.25in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1.25in; text-align: justify">The Company has a long-standing distribution
arrangement with Tuteur for distribution of GLASSIA and KAMRHO(D) in Argentina and several other South American countries. The original
agreement was entered into in November 2001 and since was amended, restated several times, including being replaced by a new distribution
agreement from May 2020, which was also amended several times since.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1.25in; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1.25in; text-align: justify">Tuteur was considered a related party
until November 2023, and upon departure of Mr. Jonathan Hahn from the Company&#8217;s Board of Director it is no longer treated as such.</p>

Pursuant to the Saol APA, the Company agreed to pay up to $50,000 thousand of contingent consideration subject the achievement of sales thresholds for the period commencing on the acquisition date and ending on December 31, 2034. Through December 31, 2024, the first two sales thresholds were met, and the Company paid two $3,000 thousands on account of these thresholds These payments were accounted for as a reduction of the liability. The Company may be entitled for up to $3,000 thousand credit deductible from the contingent consideration payments due for the years 2023 through 2027, subject to certain conditions as defined in the Saol APA. During 2023 and 2024, the entitlement of the credit was not met.
The fair value of the contingent consideration was $23,566 thousand and $21,855 thousand as of December 31, 2024, and December 31, 2023, respectively. The Company accounted for $4,711 thousand, $1,321 thousand, and $1,539 thousand, for the years ended December 31, 2024, 2023 and 2022, respectively as financing expenses in the statement of profit and loss to reflects the changes in the fair value of the liability.</ix:footnote><!--Text not found in footnote sections assigned to Schedule of Financial Liabilities Assumed through Business Combinations-->
